old_digest: Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. When there shall be less than five players on a side.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_digest: If one run is attempted and the batsman is run out the “No Ball” alone counts If runs are made off a “No Ball,” although the runs are scored and not the “No Ball,” the bowler is allowed another delivery.
new_digest: If one run is attempted and the batsman is run out the “No Ball” alone counts. If runs are made off a “No Ball,” although the runs are scored and not the “No Ball,” the bowler is allowed another delivery.

In 1911 an agreement was arrived at between the Counties that “Trial balls, if both batsmen are at the wickets, be not allowed in First Class Matches.” This arrangement was approved and adopted by the M.C.C.

old_digest: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.” 9
new_digest: If the batsman is in the act of jumping in the air and the bat is also off the ground he would be “out of his ground.”

old_digest: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_digest: A Batsman may be out l b w, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.
new_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an l b w with a breaking ball.

old_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.” 11
new_digest: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.”

old_digest: It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets—the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the bail had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.
new_digest: It would not be out if the striker hit the ball into the opposite wickets —the other batsman being out of his ground—unless the ball had been touched by a fieldsman after being hit and before striking the wickets.

old_digest: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught.
new_digest: When a run has been made oft’ a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught.

old_digest: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball,” when the ball shall be “Dead”; six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have been run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_digest: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball,” when the ball shall be “Dead”; six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have boon run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_digest: He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
new_digest: He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking oft’ the bails.

old_digest: The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease. --2 7
new_digest: The responsibility of supervising the rolling of the pitch before play will, in the first place, rest with the Umpires. The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease.
